review_telemetry.what: EVERY dispatch of this spec's own reviews - verdict rounds and transport failures alike - taken from the `usage` object each codex-exec run emits, not estimated. A timed-out attempt emits no usage and is recorded with null fields rather than omitted, so the counts below and the CHANGELOG agree. All of them ran through the shipped fetch-not-embed path.

demonstrated: The dispatched prompt is 83.17% smaller on this spec's own review range (70,243 -> 11,824 bytes), measured by assembling both prompt shapes from the same git reads.
The scope map is complete and resolvable where it previously was not: `--stat` elided 28 of 43 paths here; `--numstat --no-renames -z` elides 0 at effectively the same byte cost (2,769 vs 2,823).
The reviewer now works from 100% of the diff instead of the ~10% that fit under the old 50 KB embed cap.
Every finding across 7 verdict rounds cited a resolvable repository path, which is the property the scope map exists to enable.
3 of 10 dispatches hit the fixed 600s exec timeout and every one was recorded as a transport failure with its round refunded, so the cap accounting survived the slower fetch pattern intact.
NOT_demonstrated: A reduction in TOTAL review token cost. Input tokens for these rounds ran 3,487,600-5,554,695, ABOVE the 544k-1.12M recorded for fn-168's pre-identity impl reviews. The fetch model moves cost off the prompt and onto conversation turns: the reviewer makes many tool calls and each turn resends the accumulated context. 91-96% of that input is CACHED, so billable cost does not scale with the raw number, but this measurement does not establish a cheaper review and no doc may claim one.

The comparison is also confounded: this spec's diff is larger than fn-168's, it took more rounds, and the reviewer was asked to verify deletions across ~2,000 lines. A clean cost comparison needs the same diff reviewed both ways, which this spec did not run.
honest_reading.operational_note: The exec timeout was 600s hardcoded and was reached 3 times across 10 dispatches on this spec's large diff, because a fetching reviewer spends wall-clock on tool calls that an embedded prompt spent on nothing. Each was correctly recorded as a transport failure with the round refunded, and narrowing the review base made the retry succeed. fn-169 raised the bound to 1800s and made it env-overridable (FLOW_REVIEW_EXEC_TIMEOUT); that buys headroom but does not fix the SHAPE - a wall-clock bound cannot tell a reviewer that is working from a process that is wedged. An idle deadline can, because `codex exec --json` streams events. Captured as .flow/tmp/fn-170-idle-liveness-CAPTURE.md.
